# cybercore-charts

> Zero-dependency SVG chart library with a cyberpunk look: line and area, bar, donut and pie, gauge, sparkline. TypeScript, React and Ember adapters, accessible by default, themed by cybercore-css tokens with built-in fallbacks.

Every code block in this file is type-checked against the library's sources (`bin/docs-check`), so the options, methods and imports shown here exist. Types are the source of truth: `src/types.ts`.

- npm: `cybercore-charts` (version 0.2.0 in this file's CDN URLs)
- Demo and playgrounds: https://sebyx07.github.io/cybercore-charts/
- Repository: https://github.com/sebyx07/cybercore-charts
- Companion CSS framework: https://github.com/sebyx07/cybercore-css

## Rules for generated code

1. A chart needs a container element that exists in the DOM. Pass the element or a CSS selector.
2. Create charts in the browser, after mount. Importing the package on a server is safe; creating a chart without a DOM throws an error containing "requires a DOM".
3. Call `chart.destroy()` when the container goes away. The React components and the Ember modifier do it for you.
4. New data: `chart.update(data)`. New options: `chart.setOptions({ theme: 'magenta' })`. Do not destroy and recreate for either.
5. `theme` is one of `'accent'` (default), `'cyan'`, `'magenta'`, `'green'`, `'yellow'`. There are no other theme names and no theme factory: restyle with CSS custom properties (see Theming).
6. Chart types are `'line'`, `'bar'`, `'donut'`, `'gauge'`, `'sparkline'`. An area chart is a line chart with `showArea: true`; a pie is a donut with `innerRadius: 0`. There is no scatter or radar chart.
7. Give each chart an `ariaLabel` that says what it shows.
8. Sizes are in pixels. Use `responsive: true` and size the container with CSS to follow the layout.

## Install

```bash
npm install cybercore-charts
```

Entry points:

| Import | Contents |
|---|---|
| `cybercore-charts` | `createChart`, the chart classes, types, helpers (ESM and CommonJS) |
| `cybercore-charts/react` | React components and hooks (React 18 or later, optional peer) |
| `cybercore-charts/ember` | the `cyberChart` modifier (Ember 5 or later with `ember-modifier` 4 or later, optional peers) |
| `cybercore-charts/styles` | the optional stylesheet, as SCSS source |
| `cybercore-charts/umd` | the minified browser bundle that defines the `CyberCharts` global |

## Quick start

```html
<div id="traffic" style="height: 280px"></div>
```

```ts
import { createChart } from 'cybercore-charts';

const chart = createChart('line', '#traffic', {
  data: [
    { x: 'Mon', y: 12 },
    { x: 'Tue', y: 30 },
    { x: 'Wed', y: 18 },
  ],
  ariaLabel: 'Requests per day',
  showArea: true,
  responsive: true,
});

chart.update([
  { x: 'Mon', y: 14 },
  { x: 'Tue', y: 26 },
  { x: 'Wed', y: 31 },
]);
chart.setOptions({ theme: 'magenta' });
chart.destroy();
```

`createChart(type, container, options)` returns the chart instance. The classes take the same arguments: `new LineChart(container, options)`.

## Options shared by line, bar, donut and gauge (`BaseChartOptions`)

| Option | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `width` | number | 400 (donut, gauge: 300) | pixels |
| `height` | number | 300 | pixels |
| `padding` | `{ top, right, bottom, left }`, each optional | 20, 20, 40, 50 | space around the plot |
| `theme` | `ChartTheme` | `'accent'` | chart colour |
| `animate` | boolean | true | entry animation; always off under reduced motion |
| `animation` | `AnimationConfig` | | `enabled`, `duration` (ms), `easing`, `delay`, `stagger` |
| `tooltip` | `TooltipConfig` | enabled | `enabled`, `formatter(point, series)` returning text, `followCursor` |
| `glow` | boolean or `GlowConfig` | true | neon glow filter; `GlowConfig` has `enabled`, `intensity`, `blur`, `useThemeColor` |
| `scanlines` | boolean | false | decorative scanline overlay |
| `classPrefix` | string | `'cyber-chart'` | BEM block of the generated classes |
| `responsive` | boolean | false | follow the container's size |
| `ariaLabel` | string | chart name | accessible name (the SVG `<title>`) |
| `description` | string | generated | accessible description (the SVG `<desc>`) |
| `dataTable` | boolean | true (gauge: false) | visually hidden data table for screen readers |
| `keyboard` | boolean | true (gauge: false) | data marks reachable with the keyboard |
| `locale` | string | runtime locale | BCP 47 locale for numbers and dates |

Easing names: `'linear'`, `'easeIn'`, `'easeOut'`, `'easeInOut'`, `'easeInCubic'`, `'easeOutCubic'`, `'easeInOutCubic'`.

## Line chart

```ts
import { LineChart } from 'cybercore-charts';
import type { DataSeries } from 'cybercore-charts';

const series: DataSeries[] = [
  {
    id: 'down',
    name: 'Download',
    data: [
      { x: 'Jan', y: 100 },
      { x: 'Feb', y: 150 },
    ],
  },
  {
    id: 'up',
    name: 'Upload',
    theme: 'magenta',
    data: [
      { x: 'Jan', y: 80 },
      { x: 'Feb', y: 120 },
    ],
  },
];

const line = new LineChart('#traffic', {
  data: series,
  ariaLabel: 'Traffic by month',
  interpolation: 'smooth',
  showArea: true,
  areaOpacity: 0.2,
  showPoints: true,
  pointRadius: 4,
  lineWidth: 2,
  connectNulls: false,
  maxPoints: 1000,
  xAxis: { show: true, showGrid: true, showLabels: true, ticks: 5, label: 'Month' },
  yAxis: { min: 0, formatLabel: (value) => `${value} GB` },
  legend: { show: true },
  tooltip: { formatter: (point, s) => `${s ? s.name : 'Value'}: ${point.y} GB` },
});
```

| Option | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `data` | `DataPoint[]` or `DataSeries[]` | required |
| `showArea` | boolean | false |
| `areaOpacity` | number, 0 to 1 | 0.2 |
| `showPoints` | boolean | true |
| `pointRadius` | number | 4 |
| `lineWidth` | number | 2 |
| `interpolation` | `'linear'`, `'smooth'`, `'step'`, `'stepBefore'`, `'stepAfter'` | `'linear'` |
| `xAxis`, `yAxis` | `AxisConfig` | shown, 5 ticks |
| `legend` | `LegendConfig` | shown for several series |
| `connectNulls` | boolean | false |
| `maxPoints` | number | 1000 |
| `simplifyTolerance` | number | 1 |

- `DataPoint` is `{ x, y, label?, color?, meta? }`; `x` is a number, a string or a `Date`. Dates get a time scale.
- `DataSeries` is `{ id, name, data, theme?, color?, visible? }`.
- `AxisConfig`: `show`, `showGrid`, `showLabels`, `min`, `max`, `ticks`, `formatLabel`, `label`. Without `min` and `max` the axis follows the data with rounded ticks.
- A `y` that is `NaN` or infinite leaves a gap in the line; `connectNulls: true` bridges it.
- Series longer than `maxPoints` are simplified before drawing; `0` turns that off.

## Bar chart

```ts
import { BarChart } from 'cybercore-charts';

const bar = new BarChart('#latency', {
  data: [
    { x: 'api', y: 45 },
    { x: 'db', y: 72 },
    { x: 'cache', y: 8 },
  ],
  ariaLabel: 'Latency by service, in milliseconds',
  orientation: 'horizontal',
  groupMode: 'grouped',
  borderRadius: 2,
  barGap: 0.1,
  groupGap: 0.2,
  showValues: true,
  valuePosition: 'outside',
});
```

| Option | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `data` | `DataPoint[]` or `DataSeries[]` | required |
| `orientation` | `'vertical'`, `'horizontal'` | `'vertical'` |
| `groupMode` | `'grouped'`, `'stacked'` | `'grouped'` |
| `borderRadius` | number | 2 |
| `barGap` | number, 0 to 1 | 0.1 |
| `groupGap` | number, 0 to 1 | 0.2 |
| `showValues` | boolean | false |
| `valuePosition` | `'inside'`, `'outside'`, `'center'` | `'outside'` |
| `xAxis`, `yAxis`, `legend` | as for the line chart | |

## Donut and pie chart

```ts
import { DonutChart } from 'cybercore-charts';

const donut = new DonutChart('#storage', {
  data: [
    { label: 'Logs', value: 35 },
    { label: 'Media', value: 25, theme: 'magenta' },
    { label: 'Backups', value: 40, color: '#ffb000' },
  ],
  ariaLabel: 'Storage by kind',
  innerRadius: 0.6,
  segmentGap: 2,
  showLabels: true,
  showPercentages: true,
  centerText: '100 GB',
  centerSubtext: 'used',
  sortSegments: 'desc',
});

donut.getTotal();
```

| Option | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `data` | `DonutSegment[]`: `{ label, value, color?, theme?, meta? }` | required |
| `innerRadius` | number, 0 (pie) to below 1 | 0.6 |
| `segmentGap` | degrees | 2 |
| `showLabels` | boolean | true |
| `labelPosition` | `'inside'`, `'outside'` | `'outside'` |
| `showPercentages` | boolean | true |
| `centerText`, `centerSubtext` | string | empty |
| `startAngle` | degrees | -90 |
| `sortSegments` | boolean, `'asc'`, `'desc'` | false |
| `legend` | `LegendConfig` | shown |

## Gauge

```ts
import { GaugeChart } from 'cybercore-charts';

const gauge = new GaugeChart('#load', {
  value: 72,
  min: 0,
  max: 100,
  label: 'CPU load',
  ariaLabel: 'CPU load',
  thickness: 20,
  showTicks: true,
  tickCount: 10,
  thresholds: [
    { value: 60, theme: 'green' },
    { value: 85, theme: 'yellow' },
    { value: 100, theme: 'magenta' },
  ],
  formatValue: (value) => `${Math.round(value)}%`,
});

gauge.update(81);
gauge.getValue();
```

| Option | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | number | required |
| `min`, `max` | number | 0, 100 |
| `startAngle`, `endAngle` | degrees | -135, 135 |
| `thickness` | number | 20 |
| `showValue` | boolean | true |
| `formatValue` | `(value) => string` | rounded number |
| `showMinMax` | boolean | true |
| `label` | string | empty |
| `thresholds` | `GaugeThreshold[]`: `{ value, color?, theme?, label? }` | none |
| `showTicks`, `tickCount` | boolean, number | true, 10 |

`update()` takes the new value. The gauge is exposed to assistive technology as a meter.

## Sparkline

```ts
import { Sparkline } from 'cybercore-charts';

const spark = new Sparkline('#trend', {
  data: [5, 10, 8, 15, 12, 18, 14],
  ariaLabel: 'Sign-ups, last 7 days',
  width: 120,
  height: 32,
  lineWidth: 1.5,
  showArea: true,
  showEndPoint: true,
  showMinMax: false,
  interpolation: 'smooth',
});

spark.getStats();
```

`SparklineOptions` is its own, smaller set: `data` (numbers, required), `width` (120), `height` (32), `theme`, `color`, `lineWidth` (1.5), `showArea` (false), `areaOpacity` (0.2), `showEndPoint` (true), `showMinMax` (false), `glow` (true), `interpolation` (`'linear'` or `'smooth'`), `animate` (true), `animationDuration` (500), `ariaLabel`, `description`, `locale`. `getStats()` returns `{ min, max, first, last, trend }`; `getData()` returns the numbers.

## Instance methods

Every chart has these:

| Method | Does |
|---|---|
| `update(data)` | draws new data (the gauge takes a number) |
| `setOptions(options)` | changes options in place |
| `resize(width, height)` | sets a new size; both arguments optional |
| `getSVG()` | the `SVGSVGElement` |
| `toSVG()` | the chart as an SVG string |
| `on(event, handler)` | subscribes |
| `off(event, handler)` | unsubscribes; without a handler, every handler of that event |
| `destroy()` | removes the chart and everything it created |

## Events

```ts
import { createChart } from 'cybercore-charts';
import type { ChartEvent, DataPoint, DataSeries } from 'cybercore-charts';

const chart = createChart('bar', '#latency', { data: [{ x: 'api', y: 45 }] });

chart.on('barClick', (event: ChartEvent<{ point: DataPoint; series: DataSeries }>) => {
  console.log(event.data.point.x, event.data.point.y, event.data.series.name);
});
```

| Event | Emitted by | `event.data` |
|---|---|---|
| `pointHover`, `pointClick` | line | `{ point, series }` |
| `barHover`, `barClick` | bar | `{ point, series }` |
| `segmentHover`, `segmentClick` | donut | the `DonutSegment` |
| `resize` | every chart | the new size |

`legendClick` is in the `ChartEventType` union and is not emitted by any chart yet. A click event also fires for Enter and Space on a focused mark; `event.originalEvent` is then undefined.

## React

```tsx
import { useRef } from 'react';
import { CyberGaugeChart, CyberLineChart } from 'cybercore-charts/react';
import type { CyberLineChartRef } from 'cybercore-charts/react';

const points = [
  { x: 'Mon', y: 12 },
  { x: 'Tue', y: 30 },
];

export function Dashboard() {
  const line = useRef<CyberLineChartRef>(null);

  return (
    <>
      <CyberLineChart
        ref={line}
        data={points}
        ariaLabel="Requests per day"
        showArea
        responsive
        style={{ height: 280 }}
        onPointClick={(event) => console.log(event.data)}
      />
      <CyberGaugeChart value={72} label="CPU load" ariaLabel="CPU load" />
      <button type="button" onClick={() => console.log(line.current?.toSVG())}>
        Export SVG
      </button>
    </>
  );
}
```

- Components: `CyberLineChart`, `CyberBarChart`, `CyberDonutChart`, `CyberGaugeChart`, `CyberSparkline`. Every option of the matching chart is a prop; any other prop (a class name, a style, an id, data attributes) goes to the container `<div>`.
- Event props: `onPointHover`, `onPointClick` (line); `onBarHover`, `onBarClick` (bar); `onSegmentHover`, `onSegmentClick` (donut); `onResize`.
- The ref (`ChartHandle`) has `update`, `setOptions`, `resize`, `getSVG`, `toSVG` and `getChart`.
- The chart is created after mount, updated in place when props change, destroyed on unmount. Server rendering emits the empty container.
- Hooks for custom wrappers: `useChart`, `useChartInstance`.

## Ember

```gts
import { cyberChart } from 'cybercore-charts/ember';

<template>
  <div {{cyberChart "line" data=@points showArea=true responsive=true ariaLabel="Requests per day"}}></div>
</template>
```

Classic templates: re-export the modifier once as `app/modifiers/cyber-chart.js`, then use it by its dashed name.

```js
export { default } from 'cybercore-charts/ember';
```

```hbs
<div {{cyber-chart "gauge" value=this.load max=100 label="Load" onCreated=this.keepChart}}></div>
```

The first argument is the chart type; every named argument is an option of that chart, an event handler (`onPointClick`, `onBarClick`, `onSegmentClick`, `onResize` and the hover ones) or a lifecycle callback (`onCreated`, `onWillDestroy`, each called with the chart instance).

## Script tag (no build step)

```html
<div id="chart" style="height: 280px"></div>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/cybercore-charts@0.2.0/dist/cybercore-charts.umd.min.js"></script>
<script>
  const chart = CyberCharts.createChart('donut', '#chart', {
    data: [
      { label: 'Logs', value: 35 },
      { label: 'Media', value: 65 },
    ],
    ariaLabel: 'Storage by kind',
  });
  console.log(CyberCharts.VERSION, CyberCharts.colors.themeColor('magenta'));
</script>
```

The global has `createChart`, `LineChart`, `BarChart`, `DonutChart`, `GaugeChart`, `Sparkline`, `colors` (the palette and colour helpers), `utils` (math helpers and `formatNumber`) and `VERSION`.

## Theming

Colours are CSS custom properties with built-in fallbacks, so a chart follows [cybercore-css](https://github.com/sebyx07/cybercore-css) when that stylesheet is on the page and renders the same neon palette when it is not. Overrides apply live, on `:root` or on any ancestor of the chart:

```css
.sidebar {
  --color-accent: #ffb000;
  --cyber-magenta-500: #ff3d8b;
  --color-text-secondary: #d0d4dc;
  --font-mono: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
}
```

| Token | Used for |
|---|---|
| `--color-accent`, `--color-accent-light`, `--color-accent-dark` | the `'accent'` theme |
| `--cyber-cyan-500`, `--cyber-magenta-500`, `--cyber-green-500`, `--cyber-yellow-500` (and the 300 and 700 steps) | the named themes |
| `--cyber-violet-500`, `--cyber-amber-500` | later series in the series palette |
| `--color-text-secondary`, `--color-text-muted` | labels and legend |
| `--color-border-strong`, `--color-border-default` | axis and grid lines |
| `--color-bg-primary` | chart surface |
| `--color-bg-elevated`, `--color-border-accent`, `--color-text-primary` | tooltip |
| `--focus-ring-color` | keyboard focus ring |
| `--font-mono` | chart typeface |

With cybercore-css, `data-theme="magenta"` on an ancestor retints every `'accent'` chart inside it. Per chart: `theme`, or `color` on a series, a point, a segment or a threshold.

Helpers: `themeColor(theme, shade)` and `seriesColor(index)` return the `var(--token, fallback)` strings the charts use; `SERIES_PALETTE` is the series order; `uiColors` holds the non-data colours; `cyberColors` is the fallback palette.

The stylesheet is optional polish (hover states, tooltip and legend styling):

```scss
@use 'cybercore-charts/styles';
```

## Accessibility

- The root SVG has a `<title>` (`ariaLabel`) and a `<desc>` (`description`, or a generated summary of the data).
- A visually hidden table of the data follows the chart (`dataTable`, up to 500 rows).
- Keyboard (`keyboard`): one tab stop per chart, arrow keys and Home/End move between marks, Enter or Space activates, Escape closes the tooltip. Each mark has a label.
- Reduced motion: no animation when the system asks for it or an ancestor has `data-motion="reduce"`.
- Higher contrast: when the system asks for it or an ancestor has `data-contrast="high"`.
- Series colours are ordered to stay distinguishable with the common forms of colour blindness, and series are always named in the legend, the tooltip and the table.

## Server rendering

Importing any entry point in Node is safe. Charts are created in the browser: in React the components handle it; elsewhere create the chart in your framework's mount hook. `chart.toSVG()` returns markup you can save or inline once the chart exists.

## TypeScript

```ts
import type {
  BarChartOptions,
  BaseChartOptions,
  ChartEvent,
  ChartEventHandler,
  ChartEventType,
  ChartInstance,
  ChartTheme,
  DataPoint,
  DataSeries,
  DonutChartOptions,
  DonutSegment,
  GaugeChartOptions,
  GaugeThreshold,
  LineChartOptions,
  SparklineOptions,
} from 'cybercore-charts';
```

Custom charts extend the exported `BaseChart`; the extension points are described in `src/CLAUDE.md` in the repository.

## Browser support

Current Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari. The ES module and CommonJS builds target ES2022, the UMD bundle ES2020; `responsive` needs `ResizeObserver`. Node 18 or later for importing on a server.
